chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered Mecca on the day he conquered it, he opened the door of the Ka'bah and ordered that the images in the Ka'bah be obliterated. Then he took hold of the two hinges of the door and said: 'There is no god but Allah, Alone, with no partner. He fulfilled His promise and helped His servant and defeated the confederates alone. What are you saying and what do you think?' They said: 'We think good and we say good, O noble brother and noble cousin's son, and you have gained power.' He said: 'So I say as my brother Yusuf said: No reproach upon you today; may Allah forgive you, and He is the most merciful of the merciful. Indeed, Allah has made Mecca sacred from the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by the sanctity of Allah until the Day of Resurrection. its game is not driven away, its trees are not cut, its dry grass is not gathered, and its lost items are not picked up except by one who announces it.' Al-Abbas said: 'O Messenger of Allah, except for al-idhkhir, for it is for the grave and the houses.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Except for al-idhkhir.'

key_terms.إِذْخِرَ: A type of fragrant grass used for graves and houses
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: The Ka'bah, the cube-shaped building in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What are the specific legal rulings regarding the sanctity of Mecca established during the Conquest?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s (s) declaration of Mecca’s eternal sanctity upon its conquest, linking the physical purification of the Ka'bah from idols to the spiritual principle of 'no reproach' (La Thrība 'Alaykum) from Surah Yusuf. It establishes the enduring legal status of the Haram, prohibiting hunting, tree-cutting, and collecting lost items, with a specific exception for Idhkhir noted by Al-Abbas. This narrative underscores the continuity of Mecca’s sacred status from creation to the Day of Judgment, reinforcing its unique position in Islamic jurisprudence.
